judged_text: The service passes credentialId (the credential row id) as refreshOAuthTokens' third parameter, which is documented and used as the cal.com user id in the sync request body. With sync enabled, the parent endpoint receives the credential's DB id as calcomUserId — it either fails to resolve a user or returns a different user's OAuth tokens, which are then stored under this credential, cross-linking another user's integration access or breaking Zoho Bigin sync entirely.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, the 3rd parameter is clearly treated as a Cal.com *user id* (`calcomUserId: userId.toString()` in the POST body). However, in `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new call passes `credentialId` as that 3rd argument (`refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)`). From the diff we can’t see `credentialId`’s definition, but the finding’s claim is consistent with the name and contrasts with other updated integrations which pass `credential.userId`. With credential sync enabled (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), this would send a credential row id as `calcomUserId`, causing failed user lookup or wrong token association at the parent endpoint.
